chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Ali ibn Ribat, from Ibn Muskan, from Lays al-Murady, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the fasting person who gets cupping done and pours oil into his ear. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem, except for the snuff, for it is disliked.'

key_terms.السُّعُوطَ: the snuff (powder sniffed into the nose)

ai.seo_question: Does cupping or putting oil in the ear break the fast in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of nullifiers by distinguishing between external applications and internal absorption. While cupping and ear oil are deemed permissible, the specific dislike of *su'oot* (snuff) highlights the scholarly concern that sniffing may carry particles deep enough to reach the stomach, thereby affecting the fast's validity. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of caution regarding substances that traverse the throat to the stomach during daylight hours.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Husayn, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from his father, from Ali Bin Rabaat, from Ibn Muskan, from Lays Al Murady who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Fasting one who gets cupping done, and he pours the oil into his ears. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem except for the snuff, for it is disliked’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn al-Hassan from his father from Ali ibn Ribat from ibn Muskan from Layth al-Muradiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a fasting man who applies cupping and oil in his ears. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful except sniffing snuff, which is undesirable.’”
